payroll.heading: Payroll
payroll.intro: Hours and pay per worker for one period. The total and the rows are cut by the same dates, on the server. Check the notes below before you transfer anything — a shift only counts once its end time is confirmed.
payroll.attributionHint: A shift counts in the period it started in, even if it ended after midnight.
payroll.caveatUnresolved: {count, plural, one {# shift needs confirming before this total is final. It was closed by the 8-hour timer, so the hours below leave it out.} other {# shifts need confirming before this total is final. They were closed by the 8-hour timer, so the hours below leave them out.}}
payroll.caveatOpen: {count, plural, one {# shift in this period is still open and has no end time, so it is not counted.} other {# shifts in this period are still open and have no end time, so they are not counted.}}
payroll.caveatNoneExcluded: No shift in this period is open or waiting to be confirmed, so nothing has been left out for those reasons.
payroll.caveatTruncated: Only the {limit} most recent shifts were loaded and the oldest of them starts on {earliest}. This period reaches further back, so the totals below are INCOMPLETE and too low.
payroll.caveatReconcile: The server's own total for this period is {server} but the shifts loaded here add up to {visible}. The difference is work that exists in the database and was not sent to this screen because the row limit cut it off, so this total is too low.
payroll.caveatReconcileOk: The shifts loaded here add up to exactly the server's own total for the same period, so nothing is missing from this screen.
payroll.caveatManual: {count, plural, one {# shift in this total was entered by hand} other {# shifts in this total were entered by hand}} instead of being tapped on a tag. They are paid in full; the tag log has no record of them.
payroll.caveatOrphan: Some shifts refer to a worker that was not sent with them and have been left out of every total. Report this — it should not be possible.
payroll.caveatRateHistory: Known limitation: only one hourly rate per worker is stored, so past hours are priced at today's rate. Changing a rate changes what earlier periods appear to have cost.
payroll.emptyBody: No hours were recorded in this period.
payroll.emptyNeverRecorded: No shift has ever been recorded, in any period. Nothing is missing — nobody has tapped a tag yet.
payroll.emptyLatestRecorded: Your records are intact: the most recent shift is from {date}. This period simply contains none of them.
payroll.tableCaption: Hours and pay per worker for {period}
payroll.excludedUnresolved: {count, plural, one {# needs confirming} other {# need confirming}}
payroll.excludedOpen: {count, plural, one {# still open} other {# still open}}
payroll.exported: The CSV file has been downloaded.
payroll.exportFailed: The file could not be downloaded. Please try again.
payroll.csvTotalNoRate: {count, plural, one {Total excludes # worker with no hourly rate: no amount is calculated for those hours, not even €0.00. The hours above are complete, the amounts are not.} other {Total excludes # workers with no hourly rate: no amounts are calculated for those hours, not even €0.00. The hours above are complete, the amounts are not.}}
payroll.question: What has to be paid out this month?
payroll.answerHoursSub: Only shifts with a confirmed end time
payroll.answerExcludedNone: No shift is open or unconfirmed
payroll.answerExcludedNoRate: {count, plural, one {# worker with no hourly rate} other {# workers with no hourly rate}}
payroll.caveatNoRate: {count, plural, one {# worker has no hourly rate on file. The hours are recorded and the name is in the table below; no amount is calculated at all — not even €0.00. The payout total is therefore short by that pay.} other {# workers have no hourly rate on file. Their hours are recorded and their names are in the table below; no amounts are calculated at all — not even €0.00. The payout total is therefore short by that pay.}}

payroll.scopedWorker: This view is restricted to one person: {name}.

login.heading: Sign in
login.intro: Enter your administrator credentials to continue.
login.failed: Username or password is not right. Please try again.

workers.heading: Workers
workers.emailHint: This must match the address Apple gives us. If the worker chose “Hide My Email”, their first sign-in is refused and the app shows them the private relay address — enter that address here.
workers.phoneHint: How you reach this person. It is NOT the app sign-in — only the email address above lets someone into the app, and a phone number entered there will never work.
workers.fieldActive: Active — may sign in and record hours
workers.errorEmailShape: That is not a valid email address.
workers.errorEmailTaken: A worker with this email address already exists.
workers.errorPhoneShape: Enter a phone number using digits, spaces, +, ( ), / and - only.
workers.errorRateInvalid: Enter an amount in euros, for example 14.50.
workers.errorRejected: The server rejected these details. Please check the fields and try again.
workers.tableCaption: Workers, active ones first, then by name.
workers.codeStandingNote: An enrolment code is shown once only, at the moment you create it, and can never be looked up again — write it down or copy it straight away. If it gets lost, simply create a new one. The code is the second way into the app: on an iPhone the worker still signs in with Apple using the email address above, on any other phone they type this code once instead. The email address is therefore still needed.
workers.codeExplain: {name} types this code into the app once, the first time they open it — after that their phone is signed in and they can record hours.
workers.codeValidUntil: Valid until {expires}. After that create a new one.
workers.codeOnce: This is the only time the code is shown. If it reaches the wrong person, press “Block enrolment code” — it stops working immediately.
workers.codeCopied: Enrolment code copied to the clipboard.
workers.codeCopyFailed: Could not copy the enrolment code. Select it above and copy it manually.
workers.codeIssueFailed: The enrolment code could not be created. Please try again.
workers.codeRevoked: {name}’s enrolment code has been blocked and no longer works.
workers.codeRevokeFailed: The enrolment code could not be blocked. Please try again.
workers.question: Who works for us, and who cannot get in yet?
workers.emptyBodyNew: No workers yet. Choose “Add a worker” at the top right to file the first person.
workers.noRate: No hourly rate — named as an exclusion in payroll, not priced at €0.00
workers.rateOptionalHint: Leave empty if nothing has been agreed yet. Without a rate this person is listed in payroll by name as an exclusion and counted: the hours stay on the row, the amount reads “Not priced” and is missing from the payout total. They are never quietly paid €0.00. Fill it in as soon as the rate is settled.
workers.revokeConfirmBody: The code stops working immediately and cannot be restored. A new code can be created for this person at any time.
workers.reissueConfirmTitle: Create a new enrolment code for {name}?
workers.reissueConfirmBody: The previous code stops working from this moment, even if it has already been passed on. The new code is shown only once.
workers.deactivateConfirmBody: This person can no longer sign in or record hours. Shifts already recorded stay exactly as they are, and the person can be reactivated at any time.
workers.panelUnresolvedNone: None — nothing is holding up this person’s pay.
workers.panelUnresolvedSome: {count, plural, one {# shift, not payable until confirmed} other {# shifts, not payable until confirmed}}
workers.panelTruncated: Only the most recent shifts were loaded, so the list below may be incomplete.
workers.panelRecentEmpty: No completed shift has been recorded for this person yet.
workers.panelRecentCaption: The most recently completed shifts of {name}, newest first.
workers.panelRateHistory: Only one hourly rate is stored per worker. Changing it re-values past hours at the new rate.
workers.panelLinkShifts: All shifts of this person · all periods
workers.panelLinkUnresolved: {count, plural, one {Confirm # shift · all periods} other {Confirm # shifts · all periods}}
workers.panelLinkNoUnresolved: No shift is waiting to be confirmed.
workers.filterNoEmail: Only workers without an email address.

locations.heading: Locations
locations.slugHint: Lower-case letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, for example stephansplatz-4. Used in this panel and in log lines only — it is never written to the tag.
locations.addressHint: Street and district, so the crew knows where to go. Optional.
locations.fieldClient: Client — the company we have the contract with
locations.clientHint: Pick the company, or add a new one right here. You do not have to leave this page.
locations.fieldContact: Point of contact at the client
locations.contactHint: The person we report to. You can give them a link to this building's cleaning history from the list below.
locations.contactNeedsClientHint: Pick or add a company first — a point of contact belongs to one company.
locations.fieldNewContact: Name of the new point of contact
locations.monthlyHint: Euros per month, for example 1200 or 1200.50. Leave it empty if you do not know it yet.
locations.targetHint: Whole hours per month, for example 40. Leave it empty if nothing was agreed.
locations.targetStored: Currently stored: {value} (h:mm). Saving replaces it with the whole hours you enter.
locations.fieldActive: Active — the tag at this building opens a shift
locations.errorSlugShape: Use lower-case letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only, starting with a letter or digit.
locations.errorSlugTaken: Another building already uses this short handle.
locations.errorClientNameRequired: Enter the name of the new company.
locations.errorContactNameRequired: Enter the name of the new point of contact.
locations.errorContactNeedsClient: Pick or add a company first — a point of contact belongs to one company.
locations.errorContactEmailShape: That is not a valid email address.
locations.errorMonthlyInvalid: Enter an amount in euros, for example 1200.50, or leave it empty.
locations.errorTargetInvalid: Enter whole hours, for example 40, or leave it empty.
locations.errorRejected: The server rejected these details. Please check the fields and try again.
locations.tagExplainer: Write the tag URL below onto the NFC tag for that building, exactly as shown. The identity of a building is its UUID — the short handle is only a label for people and is never part of the tag.
locations.tableCaption: Buildings, active ones first, then by name.
locations.clientsLink: Edit companies and points of contact
locations.truncatedNote: Only the {limit} most recent shifts were loaded, so the time for the selected month can be too low for a building with a long history.
locations.monthHint: The month the time column reports on, in YYYY-MM form (for example 2026-07). Vienna local time. The agreed target is a monthly figure, so it is compared against this month only.
locations.monthEmpty: No shift was recorded for any building in the selected month.
locations.monthNever: No shift has ever been recorded, in any month. Nothing is missing — nobody has tapped a tag yet.
locations.monthLatest: Your records are intact: the most recent shift is from {date}. The selected month simply contains none of them.
locations.monthJump: Show the month of the most recent shift
locations.colContract: Contract and time in the selected month
locations.statusInactive: Inactive — tapping the tag does not start a shift
locations.timePending: {count, plural, one {# shift in the selected month has no confirmed end time and is not counted here.} other {# shifts in the selected month have no confirmed end time and are not counted here.}}
locations.shareNoContact: Add a point of contact above to share this building's cleaning history.
locations.shareContactInactive: {name} is no longer active, so this building cannot be shared.
locations.shareInactiveBuilding: Reactivate this building to share it.
locations.shareActive: {name} can see this building's cleaning history. Shared since {date}.
locations.shareExplain: Anyone who has this link can see when this building was last cleaned, the cleaner's first name and how long it took — and nothing else. Send it to {name}.
locations.shareOnce: The link is shown only this once. If you lose it, press “New link” — the old one then stops working immediately. “Stop sharing” ends access at any time.
locations.shareCopyFailed: Could not copy the link. Select it above and copy it manually.
locations.shareStopped: Sharing for {building} has been stopped. That link no longer works.
locations.shareFailed: The link could not be created. Please try again.
locations.shareStopFailed: Sharing could not be stopped. Please try again.
locations.copied: Tag URL for {name} copied to the clipboard.
locations.copyFailed: Could not copy the tag URL for {name}. Select the URL above and copy it manually.
locations.question: Which buildings do we look after, and which tag belongs to each?
locations.emptyBodyNew: No buildings yet. Choose “Add a building” at the top right — the tag URL appears here as soon as the building is saved.
locations.stepTwoNote: Contract value and target time can be filled in later. None of it is needed to record the first shift.
locations.deactivateConfirmBody: The NFC tag at this building stops starting shifts, and any live client link to this building becomes invalid at the same moment. Shifts already recorded stay exactly as they are, and the building can be reactivated at any time.
locations.filterNoTag: Only buildings with no shift recorded.
locations.filterClientEmpty: No building here is filed under this client.

clients.heading: Clients
clients.intro: The companies we have contracts with, and the people at them we report to. You can also add both while filing a building — this screen is for correcting them afterwards.
clients.statusInactivePerson: Inactive — any link they had has been stopped
clients.fieldClientActive: Active — we currently have a contract with this company
clients.contactIntro: The person at the client we report to. Deactivating them also stops any link they were given, immediately.
clients.contactEmailHint: For your own records only. It is not a login — access to the cleaning history is given by sending a link.
clients.fieldContactActive: Active — still works at this company
clients.errorClientRequired: Choose the company this person works for.
clients.errorEmailShape: That is not a valid email address.
clients.errorRejected: The server rejected these details. Please check the fields and try again.
clients.question: Who do we work for, and who do I call there?
clients.tableCaption: Clients, each followed by that client's contacts.
clients.empty: No clients yet. Choose “Add a company” at the top right — or record one straight from the building form.
clients.confirmDeactivateBody: The person is marked inactive, and every link they were given to the cleaning history stops working immediately. Reactivating them later does not bring those links back.

shifts.heading: Shifts
shifts.rangeAll: Showing every shift loaded, with no date limit.
shifts.outsideCount: {count, plural, one {# further shift lies outside this period.} other {# further shifts lie outside this period.}}
shifts.noneBlocked: All of them count towards pay.
shifts.truncated: Only the {limit} most recent shifts were loaded. Older shifts exist and are not on this screen, so this list may be incomplete for the selected period.
shifts.createIntro: For a day that was worked but never recorded — a dead phone, or a missing tag. Pick the person, the building and the times they were really there.
shifts.createManualNotice: This shift is entered by hand, not tapped. It is paid like any other shift, but it stays marked “Entered by hand” in the log below so anyone checking payroll can tell the difference.
shifts.timeZoneHint: All times on this screen are Vienna local time (Europe/Vienna).
shifts.errorEndRequired: Enter the end time. A shift added by hand must already be finished.
shifts.errorOverlap: {worker} is already recorded at {location} from {from} to {to}. Nobody can be in two buildings at once — correct that shift instead, or change these times.
shifts.errorOverlapUnknown: This worker already has another shift covering part of this time, and it is not on this screen. Choose a longer period above to find it.
shifts.errorCreateRejected: The server rejected this shift. Check the worker, the building and the times, then try again.
shifts.correctUnresolvedNotice: This shift was closed by the 8-hour timer. Saving marks it confirmed and puts its hours into payroll — including if you leave the end time exactly as it is. Correct the end time first if it is wrong.
shifts.endHint: Enter the time the worker really left. Leave this empty to put the shift back to running — while it is empty it does not count towards pay.
shifts.errorStartInvalid: That is not a valid date and time.
shifts.errorEndInvalid: That is not a valid date and time.
shifts.errorEndBeforeStart: The end must be after the start.
shifts.errorGone: This shift no longer exists. Reload the page.
shifts.errorRejected: The server rejected this correction. Please check the times and try again.
shifts.emptyBody: No shifts recorded yet. A shift appears here as soon as a worker taps a tag.
shifts.emptyFiltered: No shifts match this filter. Try a longer period or another worker.
shifts.emptyOutside: {count, plural, one {No shift falls in the selected period, but # shift is recorded outside it. Nothing has been lost — the period is hiding it.} other {No shift falls in the selected period, but # shifts are recorded outside it. Nothing has been lost — the period is hiding them.}}
shifts.latestRecorded: The most recent recorded shift starts on {date}.
shifts.question: Which shifts need a decision?
shifts.triageMore: {count, plural, one {# more shift is only in the log below.} other {# more shifts are only in the log below.}}
shifts.linkedShiftMissing: The linked shift is not in the loaded data. It may have been corrected in the meantime.

inventory.heading: Products & Equipment
inventory.kindHint: “Product” is used up, for example floor cleaner. “Equipment” is kept and reused, for example a vacuum cleaner.
inventory.costHint: Euros for one of these, for example 4.90. Leave empty if you do not know the price yet.
inventory.fieldActive: In use — still ordered and handed out
inventory.errorCostInvalid: Enter an amount in euros, for example 4.90.
inventory.errorGone: This entry no longer exists. Reload the page.
inventory.errorRejected: The server rejected these details. Please check the fields and try again.
inventory.tableCaption: Products and equipment, in use first, then by type and name.
inventory.question: What do we have, and what does it cost?
inventory.empty: No entries yet. Choose “Add an entry” at the top right to record the first product or piece of equipment.

materials.heading: Material requests
materials.notePolling: There is no push notification anywhere in this system. The worker's app asks the server from time to time, so a request you move here reaches their screen the next time they open the app — not the moment you click.
materials.noteAttribution: The building on a request is the one the worker named. It is context for your decision and nothing more: material costs are shared across every building in proportion to the hours worked there, never charged to the building on the request.
materials.noteUnpriced: A request you have ordered but not yet priced counts as zero in the profit and loss. Enter the invoice amount when it arrives; the cost stays in the month you ordered it, so the past period corrects itself.
materials.unpricedWarning: {unpriced, plural, one {# ordered request has no cost on it yet and is counted as zero in the profit and loss.} other {# ordered requests have no cost on them yet and are counted as zero in the profit and loss.}}
materials.truncated: Only the {limit} most recent requests were loaded. Open ones are listed first, so nothing that is waiting on you is missing — but older history is cut off.
materials.filterHint: “Still open” hides requests that have been delivered or refused. Both of those are final.
materials.emptyOpen: Nothing is waiting on you. Every request has either been delivered or refused.
materials.emptyAll: No material request has ever been filed. Nothing is missing — nobody has asked for anything through the app yet.
materials.emptyShowAll: {total, plural, one {Show the # request that has already been dealt with} other {Show all # requests, including the ones already dealt with}}
materials.tableCaption: Material requests, open ones first, then newest first.
materials.itemUnmapped: Not matched to a catalogue entry yet
materials.itemMappedQuantity: {quantity, plural, one {Matched to {name}, # unit} other {Matched to {name}, # units}}
materials.timelineOrdered: Ordered {when}. The cost belongs to that month.
materials.timelineArrived: Delivered {when}. The worker's app has not picked it up yet.
materials.detailSaved: The details on {worker}'s request were saved.
materials.itemHint: Which product or device they meant. Nothing is guessed from the wording, so this stays empty until you say.
materials.errorQuantityInvalid: Please enter a whole number of one or more, or leave the field empty.
materials.costHint: Euros for the whole purchase, for example 12,90. What the invoice says, not the catalogue price. Leave it empty until you know.
materials.errorCostInvalid: Please enter an amount in euros, for example 12,90.
materials.locationHint: Context only. It does not decide which building carries the cost — that is shared out by hours worked.
materials.noteHint: For your own records. The worker does not see it.
materials.errorRejected: The server refused these details. Please check the fields and try again.
materials.errorMoved: This request has moved on since the page was loaded. The list has been reloaded — please look again.
materials.question: Who is waiting on site right now?
materials.answerDecideSub: waiting for your yes or no
materials.confirmRejectBody: Refusing is final: nothing on this request can be changed afterwards, cost included. The worker sees the refusal the next time they open the app and has to ask again if they still need it.

pl.heading: Profit and loss
pl.intro: Revenue minus labour minus materials, per building, for one period. Every figure is calculated on the server over exactly the days you choose.
pl.attributionHint: A shift counts in the period it started in, even if it ended after midnight.
pl.baselineIntro: Nothing is flagged until you say what a building ought to earn. This system has no opinion about that and will not invent one.
pl.baselineHint: For example 15 for 15%, or 12,5. A negative value is allowed: −5 means “do not lose more than 5%”, which is a real target for a building you are winning back.
pl.errorBaselineInvalid: Please enter a percentage between −100 and 100, for example 15 or 12,5.
pl.baselineCleared: Target margin removed. No building will be flagged.
pl.baselineFailed: The target margin could not be saved. Please try again.
pl.baselineUnset: No target margin is set. No building is flagged, and every assessment below reads “cannot be assessed” — which is not the same as “passed”.
pl.baselineCurrent: Current target margin: {percent}. A building below it is flagged and explained underneath.
pl.methodRates: Labour is valued at each person's CURRENT hourly rate. There is no rate history, so raising a wage changes what every past month appears to have cost.
pl.methodRatesUnknown: Labour is valued on a basis this screen does not recognise. Please report this — the figures below may not mean what they appear to.
pl.methodMaterials: Material costs are shared across buildings in proportion to the hours worked in each of them. They are not charged to the building a worker named on a request.
pl.methodMaterialPool: {priced, plural, one {# priced request} other {# priced requests}} ordered in this period, {pool} in total, shared out that way.
pl.methodUnpriced: {unpriced, plural, one {# ordered request has no cost on it and is counted as zero} other {# ordered requests have no cost on them and are counted as zero}}, so every margin below is a little too high.
pl.methodUnallocated: {amount} of materials could not be shared out at all, because no payable hours were recorded anywhere in this period. That amount is missing from every building below.
pl.methodExclusions: Shifts still waiting for a confirmed end time are left out of labour cost entirely. A building whose hours are stuck looks cheaper than it is; the count is on its row.
pl.methodUnpricedLabour: {workers, plural, one {# worker has no hourly rate on file} other {# workers have no hourly rate on file}}. {hours} of their recorded time {buildings, plural, one {at # building} other {across # buildings}} is therefore in no labour figure at all — no amount is calculated, not even €0.00. The labour cost below is short by that pay and every affected margin is correspondingly too high.
pl.methodNoContract: {buildings, plural, one {# building has no contract covering this period} other {# buildings have no contract covering this period}}. Their revenue is unknown, not zero, so they carry {cost} of cost against no income and stay out of the totals.
pl.emptyBody: There is nothing to report for this period: no building is active and none was worked in.
pl.emptyHint: Nothing has been lost. Add a building, or choose a period in which work was recorded.
pl.tableCaption: Revenue, cost and margin per building for {period}
pl.rowExcluded: {shifts, plural, one {# shift not counted — end time unconfirmed} other {# shifts not counted — end times unconfirmed}}
pl.revenuePartial: {days, plural, one {Priced for # of {periodDays} days} other {Priced for # of {periodDays} days}}
pl.labourUnpriced: {workers, plural, one {of which {hours} by # worker with no hourly rate — not priced} other {of which {hours} by # workers with no hourly rate — not priced}}
pl.assessOk: At or above the target margin
pl.assessNoContract: Cannot be assessed — no contract on file
pl.assessZeroRevenue: Cannot be assessed — the contract is worth zero
pl.assessNoBaseline: Cannot be assessed — no target margin set
pl.totalScope: {buildings, plural, one {# building with a contract} other {# buildings with a contract}}
pl.totalNotAssessable: {buildings, plural, one {# building cannot be assessed} other {# buildings cannot be assessed}}
pl.flaggedNoBaseline: No target margin is set, so nothing is flagged. Set one above and the reasoning appears here.
pl.flaggedNone: No building is below the target margin of {baseline} in this period.
pl.flaggedNoneCaveat: {buildings, plural, one {# building could not be assessed at all, which is not the same as passing.} other {# buildings could not be assessed at all, which is not the same as passing.}}
pl.whyMargin: The margin is {margin} against a target of {baseline} — {points} percentage points short.
pl.whyRevenue: {days, plural, one {Revenue {revenue}, priced for # of {periodDays} days in the period.} other {Revenue {revenue}, priced for # of {periodDays} days in the period.}}
pl.whyLabour: Labour {labour} for {hours} worked, which is {share} of revenue.
pl.whyLabourUnpriced: {workers, plural, one {{hours} of that was worked by # person with no hourly rate on file and is not in this cost at all: no amount is calculated, not even €0.00. The real labour cost is higher and the margin above is correspondingly too high.} other {{hours} of that was worked by # people with no hourly rate on file and is not in this cost at all: no amounts are calculated, not even €0.00. The real labour cost is higher and the margin above is correspondingly too high.}}
pl.whyMaterial: Materials {material}, which is {share} of revenue — shared out by hours worked, not charged directly.
pl.whyExcluded: {shifts, plural, one {# shift is not in this cost at all: its end time has never been confirmed, so {hours} of work is missing from the figure. The real cost is higher.} other {# shifts are not in this cost at all: their end times have never been confirmed, so {hours} of work is missing from the figure. The real cost is higher.}}
pl.whyOpen: {shifts, plural, one {# shift at this building is still running and is not counted.} other {# shifts at this building are still running and are not counted.}}
pl.question: Are we earning on this building?
pl.scopedNote: This view is restricted to one building. The notes under “How this page calculates” still describe the whole period and every building.

contracts.heading: Contract management
contracts.standingHeading: What this fixes, and what it does not
contracts.noteRevenueHistory: Revenue is period-correct. A price change from today leaves every earlier month valued at the price that applied then.
contracts.noteLabourNoHistory: Labour cost is NOT period-correct. Only one hourly rate per person is stored, so raising a wage still changes what every past month appears to have cost. This is a known limitation, not something you have broken.
contracts.noteDates: Dates are Vienna calendar days. A new period starting on a day makes the day before it the last one at the old price.
contracts.noteMirror: The price shown on the buildings screen is always the current period from here.
contracts.noBuildings: No buildings yet, so there is nothing to price.
contracts.buildingsCaption: Buildings with their current contract price, active ones first.
contracts.historyEmptyConsequence: Nothing has been lost. Until a price is recorded, the profit and loss reports this building's revenue as unknown rather than as zero.
contracts.closedNoUndo: Closed — a month has already been reported on this
contracts.newIntroFirst: The first price for this building. Everything from that day on is valued with it.
contracts.newIntroReplaces: The current price is {amount} per month, in force since {from}. Saving below closes that period on the day before the new one starts.
contracts.validFromHint: Vienna calendar day. It must be later than the day the current period started; the server refuses anything that would give one day two prices.
contracts.errorDateRequired: Please choose the day the new price starts.
contracts.errorDateShape: That is not a real calendar day.
contracts.errorOverlap: A contract period already covers that day. Please choose a later day.
contracts.monthlyHint: Euros per month, for example 1200 or 1200,50. Zero is allowed and means you clean this building free of charge.
contracts.errorMonthlyInvalid: Please enter an amount in euros, for example 1200,50.
contracts.targetHint: Whole hours per month, for example 40. Leave it empty if nothing is agreed.
contracts.errorTargetInvalid: Please enter whole hours, for example 40, or leave the field empty.
contracts.clientHint: Who held the contract at the time. It starts from the building's current client, which is nearly always right; change it when a building changes hands.
contracts.noteHint: Why the price changed, for example “index adjustment 2027”. Optional.
contracts.deleted: The current contract period for {building} was removed. The price before it applies again.
contracts.errorNotCurrent: Only the current period can be undone. An earlier one has already been used to value a month somebody has seen.
contracts.errorRejected: The server refused these values. Please check the fields and try again.
contracts.question: What was agreed, and since when?
contracts.confirmUndoBody: The current contract period is removed and the price before it applies again. This cannot be undone.
contracts.preselected: Opened from the building panel: the selection below is already on this building.

analytics.heading: Building analytics
analytics.monthsHint: Vienna calendar months, counted back from the end of the period on the left.
analytics.noteExclusions: Only work with a confirmed end time is counted. Shifts still waiting for one, and shifts still running, are left out and counted separately on each row.
analytics.noteTrend: The trend is arithmetic, not a forecast: the time actually worked, month by month, and the difference between the last two. With fewer than two months containing any shift there is no trend at all, which is not the same as a flat one.
analytics.noteTargetSource: The agreed time comes from the contract in force during the period. It is a monthly figure, pro-rated over the days of the period.
analytics.noteMapEquivalent: The table under the map lists every building, including those with no coordinates, which cannot be drawn. Nothing exists only on the map.
analytics.mapNoKey: This build has no Google Maps key, so no map is drawn. Everything the map would show is in the table below.
analytics.mapNoPins: {unpinned, plural, =0 {No map is drawn: there is no building to show.} one {No map is drawn: the # building listed below has no coordinates yet.} other {No map is drawn: none of the # buildings listed below has coordinates yet.}} The table names the reason for each and offers a button to try again.
analytics.mapReady: {pinned, plural, one {# building on the map.} other {# buildings on the map.}} {unpinned, plural, =0 {Every building has coordinates.} one {# building has no coordinates and is only in the table below.} other {# buildings have no coordinates and are only in the table below.}}
analytics.mapBlocked: Google refused the map key for this address. That is a setting in the Google Cloud console — either the referrer restriction or the Maps JavaScript API itself. The table below is unaffected.
analytics.mapTimeout: The map did not load within ten seconds. The table below is unaffected.
analytics.mapNetwork: The map could not be loaded — no connection, or a browser extension blocked it. The table below is unaffected.
analytics.mapTableHint: Selecting a pin opens the same panel as the “Details” button in the table.
analytics.geoNeverAttempted: Never located — no address, or nobody has asked yet
analytics.geoRetryNoPin: {name} still could not be located ({status}). Please check the address.
analytics.geoRetryNoAddress: {name} has no address to look up. Add one on the buildings screen.
analytics.geoRetryFailed: {name} could not be looked up. Please try again.
analytics.photoNoKey: No photograph: this build has no Google Maps key.
analytics.photoNoPin: No photograph: this building has no coordinates.
analytics.photoNotChecked: No photograph: Street View coverage has not been checked for this building yet.
analytics.photoDenied: No photograph: Google refused the Street View request. The Street View Static API is not enabled on this project — that is a setting in the Google Cloud console.
analytics.photoNoImagery: No photograph: Street View has no imagery at this address.
analytics.photoLoadFailed: No photograph: the image did not load.
analytics.excludedNone: Nothing — every shift in this period has a confirmed end time
analytics.excludedSome: {shifts, plural, =0 {No shift is waiting for a confirmed end time} one {# shift is waiting for a confirmed end time, {hours} in all} other {# shifts are waiting for a confirmed end time, {hours} in all}}; {open, plural, =0 {none is still running} one {# is still running} other {# are still running}}.
analytics.panelTrendHeading: {months, plural, one {The last # month} other {The last # months}}
analytics.emptyBody: No building is active and none was worked in during this period, so there is nothing to show. Nothing has been lost.
analytics.tableCaption: Time worked against time agreed per building for {period}
analytics.rowExcluded: {shifts, plural, one {# shift not counted — end time unconfirmed} other {# shifts not counted — end times unconfirmed}}
analytics.question: Where does the time go?
analytics.answerNoTargetSub: No contract with an agreed time
analytics.answerPinnedSub: {pinned, plural, =0 {none on the map} one {# on the map} other {# on the map}}

account.heading: Account
account.question: How do I change my password?
account.hint: At least {min} characters. Changing it signs out every other session.
account.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
account.tooShort: The new password needs at least {min} characters.
account.wrongCurrent: The current password is not right.
account.rejected: The new password was not accepted.
account.noReset: There is deliberately no “forgot password” here: sign-in uses a username, not an email address, and this system sends no email at all. If the password is lost, the operator resets it on the server.
